item.title: GitLab issues emergency security updates for maximum severity AI Gateway RCE flaw CVE-2026-90970
item.description:
DevOps software maintainers have distributed emergency security updates to resolve a maximum severity template sandbox escape vulnerability in self-hosted artificial intelligence services. Authenticated remote actors can execute arbitrary system commands on underlying gateway host servers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-90970 with a CVSS score of 9.9, impacts self-hosted instances of GitLab AI Gateway powering GitLab Duo. The defect resides within template rendering subroutines processing Duo Agent Platform queries. Authenticated users with access to agent workflows submit crafted template payloads to break sandbox isolation boundaries, executing operating system commands with elevated process privileges on the hosting server node. Official security bulletins urge administrators managing self-hosted AI Gateways to apply patched maintenance builds immediately.
Subverting artificial intelligence processing gateways introduces severe software supply chain exposure across enterprise development pipelines. Because AI Gateways integrate directly with source code repositories, continuous integration runners, and deployment secrets, an unauthenticated or low-privilege host takeover enables threat actors to extract repository secrets and poison production software builds.
- Force immediate maintenance upgrades across all self-hosted GitLab AI Gateway deployments to official fixed release builds. - Gate public internet access to AI Gateway management endpoints using zero trust access control proxies. - Inspect AI Gateway execution logs for unverified template evaluation calls or anomalous process spawns. - Rotate service account tokens and API keys processed within continuous integration build pipelines.
DevOps platform defense demands rapid dependency patch execution and strict template sanitization to ensure self-hosted artificial intelligence gateways remain protected against arbitrary command execution. #CodeDefence #GitLab #DevSecOps #AISecurity #SupplyChain #RCE #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Dell urges urgent patching for max severity Container Storage Modules flaws in Kubernetes environments
item.description:
Enterprise storage infrastructure security advisories published today urge immediate patching for maximum severity vulnerabilities connecting storage arrays to container orchestrators. Unauthenticated remote actors can exploit access control flaws to gain administrative authority over containerized storage volumes.
The security advisory DSA-2026-448 impacts Dell Container Storage Modules CSM linking Dell enterprise storage arrays to Kubernetes clusters. The security defects stem from improper access control and unauthenticated API endpoints handling volume orchestration tasks. Unauthenticated remote network actors transmit malformed storage provisioning queries to bypass authorization checks, obtaining full administrative control over persistent storage volumes and underlying storage array management configurations.
Subverting container storage interfaces destroys data isolation across cloud-native Kubernetes environments. Because Container Storage Modules process persistent data volumes for production microservices, an unauthenticated storage compromise allows threat actors to tamper with application databases, exfiltrate persistent storage volumes, and disrupt containerized workloads.
- Apply official security update DSA-2026-448 across all Dell Container Storage Module installations immediately. - Restrict network visibility of Kubernetes storage management API endpoints using dedicated out-of-band management subnets. - Inspect Kubernetes audit logs for unverified storage provisioning requests originating from untrusted pod networks. - Enforce strict role-based access control RBAC parameters across container storage CSI drivers and cluster nodes.
Cloud-native storage defense depends on robust API authorization enforcement and immediate patch deployment to guarantee enterprise Kubernetes storage modules remain insulated from unauthenticated takeover vectors. #CodeDefence #Dell #Kubernetes #ContainerSecurity #CloudSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #StorageSecurity

item.title: CISA expands KEV catalog and issues SIGMA rules as Citrix NetScaler zero day patches trigger appliance reboots
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog while releasing detection guidance for perimeter gateway threats. The release coincides with reports from enterprise network administrators observing unexpected appliance reboot loops following emergency zero-day patch installations.
The KEV catalog expansion includes session fixation vulnerability CVE-2026-102489 and privilege management vulnerability CVE-2026-102490 under Binding Operational Directive 26-04. Concurrently, CISA released SIGMA detection rules targeting post-exploitation activity following wild exploitation of Citrix NetScaler zero-days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772. System administrators report that applying emergency maintenance build 14.1-73.37 causes repeated appliance reboots under specific high-throughput configurations, complicating emergency mitigation timelines.
Subverting perimeter application delivery gateways exposes internal network segments to persistent intrusion threats. While emergency patching remains critical, stability issues in perimeter firmware require security teams to deploy behavioral detection rules to identify active compromise indicators without causing network outages.
- Deploy CISA SIGMA detection rules across centralized SIEM and log analysis platforms to identify NetScaler compromise indicators. - Monitor NetScaler appliance stability following emergency build installations, preparing out-of-band management rollback paths if required. - Restrict public internet access to NetScaler management portals, placing control plane interfaces on isolated management VLANs. - Perform forensic compromise checks across system access logs for unauthorized web shell implants or unverified session creation calls.
Perimeter gateway resilience requires continuous behavioral threat detection paired with careful patch verification to ensure access controllers remain stable and shielded from active wild exploitation. #CodeDefence #Citrix #NetScaler #CISA #KEV #SIGMA #ThreatHunting #NetworkSecurity #AppSec
